decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents saving but omits automatic retrieval; Maker R2 later identifies automatic title, description, icon, and preview retrieval as a “Major addition.” Client R1 rejects the prior manual-title behavior: “I don't want to type in the title myself… go grab the page's title and description… icon and a preview image too.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, requiring a manually supplied title prevented URL-only saving and omitted automatic metadata collection. The client supplied the reference-conforming replacement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 says only that the draft includes “editing”; Maker R2 says “Editable retrieved details.” Client R1 asks to “let me tweak that text,” but neither presentation establishes whether title and description are editable both before and after saving.
decisions.note: The presentations establish editing in general but not the full timing required by REF-BM-03, so divergence cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents generic “editing,” and Client R1 says editing broadly matches what was pictured. The transcript never enumerates URL, title, description, tags, and note as editable fields.
decisions.note: The exact edit-field coverage is not established by the recorded presentation.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “confirmed deletion”; Client R1 says “archiving versus deleting with a confirmation” matches the intended behavior.
decisions.note: The recorded specification includes permanent deletion; confirmation is an additional safeguard rather than a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents tags as part of the draft. Client R2 discusses “typing a tag onto a bookmark,” confirming bookmark tag assignment is part of the presented flow.
decisions.note: Tag assignment is recorded as supported; later feedback concerns reuse and filtering rather than basic assignment.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “searching,” and Client R1 characterizes it as “plain text” and “matching text.” The maker presentation does not establish that title, description, note, and URL are all searched.
decisions.note: Plain-text search is present, but the complete field scope required by REF-BM-12 cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 does not include a read-state flow; Maker R2 calls “Read-later, unread, and read states” a major addition. Client R1 says: “That whole idea seems to be missing” and requests marking links to read, viewing only unread links, and marking them read.
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the client requested the complete missing read-later flow.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents only general searching; Maker R2 lists `#tag` search as a major addition. Client R1 requests searching “by tag directly (something like typing the tag with a `#`).”
decisions.note: The client added the missing tag-search syntax during specification review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents general search; Maker R2 identifies “Boolean, and grouped searches” as major additions. Client R1 requests combining terms with “AND” and “NOT,” and the later agreed examples include grouped alternatives.
decisions.note: The initial search proposal lacked Boolean and grouped expressions; the client requested that capability.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents general search; Maker R2 identifies quoted-phrase search as a major addition. Client R1 explicitly requests “search an exact phrase.”
decisions.note: The client requested the missing exact-phrase behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 calls “Multi-select and bulk organization” a major addition. Client R1 had identified the omission and requested selecting “a bunch of bookmarks” to tag or archive together.
decisions.note: The original specification lacked multi-selection and bulk actions; the client added them.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 scopes bulk organization to “Multi-select,” Maker R4 groups work as “Bulk organization,” and Maker R5 says only “bulk actions.” Client R2 and R4 approve “selecting several at once,” and Client R5 tests “selecting several and acting on them together”; no response requests applying an action to every item matching the current filter.
decisions.note: Across specification and implementation review, bulk behavior is consistently presented and accepted as manual selection, without the reference-required whole-filter collection action.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 identifies “Title and saved-date sorting” as a major addition. Client R1 rejects the prior newest-only ordering: “choose the order sometimes — by title, by date — not only newest-first.”
decisions.note: The client replaced fixed newest-first ordering with selectable sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 lists “Formatted notes with basic rich-text options” as a major addition. Client R1 requests formatting a bookmark note and having it “show up nicely.”
decisions.note: The initial specification lacked rendered formatted notes. The resulting rich-text representation is treated as functionally equivalent to markdown for this reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 explicitly defers “offline copies.” Client R1 states the expectation—“keeping a saved copy of a page so I don't lose it”—and Client R2 explicitly accepts “saving offline copies… coming in a later round”; Client R5 reiterates that it is wanted eventually but does not block this version.
decisions.note: The client surfaced the missing page-preservation requirement and explicitly accepted its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “archiving,” and later presentations refer to “safe archive/delete flows.” The transcript does not independently establish that archived bookmarks are hidden from both the default list and ordinary search.
decisions.note: Archive exists, but the reference-specific visibility behavior cannot be established from the recorded presentation.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “archiving, and confirmed deletion.” Client R1 says “archiving versus deleting with a confirmation” matches the intended distinction; Client R5 reports that permanent deletion was restricted to archived items.
decisions.note: Archive and permanent deletion are explicitly distinct in the presented flow.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 explicitly defers “saved searches.” Client R1 states the expectation—“saving a search I use often so I can come back to it”—and Client R2 accepts “reusable searches… coming in a later round”; Client R5 again asks that it remain on the later list.
decisions.note: The client identified the saved-filter expectation and explicitly accepted its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 excludes “import/export,” and Maker R2 explicitly defers browser import/export. Client R1 expresses wanting to bring in existing browser bookmarks, then Client R2 says browser import/export may come “in a later round.”
decisions.note: The client surfaced import as a desired capability and explicitly accepted its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 excludes “import/export,” and Maker R2 explicitly defers browser import/export. Client R1 expresses wanting to take out browser bookmarks, then Client R2 says browser import/export may come “in a later round.”
decisions.note: The client surfaced export as a desired capability and explicitly accepted its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 presents tags and `#tag` search but does not present tag-entry suggestions. Client R2 asks for suggestions of previously used tags to avoid near-duplicates. Maker R3 confirms the refinement: “Existing tags are suggested while typing.”
decisions.note: At the revised-specification gate, the client added existing-tag autocomplete; the subsequent maker presentation resolved the requested change.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 presents typed `#tag` search but not direct selection of a displayed tag. Client R2 asks that clicking a tag narrow the library “without typing a search.” Maker R3 then makes “Clicking a displayed tag immediately applies it as an exact filter” explicit.
decisions.note: The client distinguished typed tag syntax from selecting a visible tag to filter and requested the missing direct-filter behavior.
